figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Trichothecene natural products. (a) Representative trichothecene structures. (b) Proposed biosynthetic pathway for the EPT core
scaffold found in all trichothecenes. (c) Byproducts observed during the acid-catalyzed nonenzymatic transformation of 2 to 4.16

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Comparative genomics analysis between different trichothecene producers. (a) Selected biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) of both
macrocyclic trichothecenes and simple trichothecenes. HP, hypothetic protein. More trichothecene BGCs are shown in Figure S2. (b)
Characterized Tri3 orthologues from simple trichothecene biosynthetic pathways.20−22

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. In vivo and in vitro functional characterization of Tri3 from macrocyclic trichothecene biosynthetic pathways. (a) Heterologous
expression of tri3 genes from two distinct macrocyclic trichothecene producers resulted in conversion of 2 to 7 and 4. (b) Tri3-catalyzed
conversion of 2 is acetyl-CoA-dependent. (c) Mass shift of 9 using isotope-labeled acetyl-CoA. (d) Nonenzymatic conversion of 9 in buffered
solution.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. In vitro activity characterization of Fusarium sporotrichioides Tri3. (a) FsTri3 catalyzes O-acetylation of isotrichotriol, which demonstrates
that Tri3 from a simple trichothecene pathway is also involved in the biosynthetic formation of the EPT skeleton. Mass-shift assay using 13C-labeled
AcCoA supports the observed intermediate 10 as isotrichotriol 11-O-acetate. (b) Summary of the unified function of Tri3 in the early-stage
biosynthesis of trichothecenes.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. In vivo and in vitro activity characterization of P. roridum Tri14. (a) Coexpression of tri3 + 4 + 5 + 14 led to the clean and efficient
production of EPT. (b) In vitro characterization of the Tri14 function in the biosynthesis of EPT 4 from isotrichodiol 2. (c) In vitro
characterization of the Tri14 function in the biosynthesis of 3-hydroxy-EPT 5 from isotrichotriol 3. (d) Revised biosynthetic mechanism for the
EPT skeleton of trichothecenes.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Biochemical study of Tri14. (a) EPT was manually docked into the putative active site pocket of an AlphaFold model of PrTri14. (b)
Activity comparison of PrTri14 mutants revealed catalytically essential residues H218 and E266. Reactions were performed in KPi buffer (pH 7.5)
with 2 mM substrate 9 and 1 μM enzyme. Reaction was incubated at 37 °C for 5 min then analyzed by LC-MS. (c) Proposed catalytic mechanism
of Tri14.
